section.content: 本公开的示例性实施例涉及用于波束管理的人工智能/机器学习（AI/ML）模型机制。在一个方面中，终端设备向网络设备发送该终端设备在监测窗口内的操作条件，在该监测窗口上，活动的人工智能/机器学习（AI/ML）模型的异常检测被执行。该终端设备然后接收来自网络设备的异常检测的结果，其中该结果基于历史数据和AI/ML模型的性能度量之间的比较。

Exemplary embodiments of the present disclosure relate to an artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) model mechanism for beam management. In one aspect, a terminal device sends operating conditions of the terminal device within a monitoring window to a network device, over which anomaly detection of an active artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) model is performed. The terminal device then receives a result of the anomaly detection from the network device, wherein the result is based on a comparison between the historical data and performance metrics of the AI/ML model.

Technical Field

Exemplary embodiments of the present disclosure relate generally to the field of communications and, in particular, relate to an apparatus, device, method, and computer-readable storage medium for improving an artificial intelligence/machine learning model (AI/ML) mechanism for beam management.

Background

A communication network may be considered a facility that enables communication between two or more communication devices, or that provides access to a data network for communication devices. A mobile or wireless communication network is one example of a communication network.

Such communication networks operate according to standards, such as those provided by 3GPP (third generation partnership project) or ETSI (european telecommunications standards institute). An example of a standard is the so-called 5G (fifth generation) standard provided by 3 GPP.

Disclosure of Invention

In general, exemplary embodiments of the present disclosure provide a solution for improving the mechanism of AI/ML models for beam management.

The application of AI/ML technology to the NR air interface has been investigated. Specification support for a generic framework for AI/ML for the air interface and enabling recommended use cases have been discussed in previous studies. In addition, multiple research objectives will address some of the prominent issues identified during the study to enhance understanding of future regulatory work. For example, specification support needs to be provided for beam management (downlink transmitter (DL TX) beam prediction for both UE-side and NW-side models) from (1) spatial domain DL TX beam prediction for beam set a ("BM-Case 1") based on measurements of beam set B, (2) temporal DL TX beam prediction for beam set a ("BM-Case 2") based on historical measurements of beam set B, (3) specifying the necessary signaling/mechanisms to facilitate LCM operation (if any) specific to the beam management use Case, and (4) enabling method(s) to ensure consistency between training and reasoning about NW-side additional conditions (if identified) for reasoning at the UE. Therefore, it is directed to a generic framework design to support both BM-Case1 and BM-Case 2.

For technical specification group radio access networks there is a study of AI/ML for NR air interfaces in release 18. The problem statement emphasizes the need for reliable AI/ML models in beam management within 3GPP networks, highlighting the importance of the fallback mechanism when these models fail. There are some proposed solutions to disclose various approaches to solving the challenges outlined in the problem statement. While the proposed solution generally addresses various aspects of the problem statement, there are still significant shortcomings in terms of specificity of implementation of thresholds, monitoring mechanisms, and fallback strategies. The advantages of these solutions vary, some providing a robust framework for monitoring and switching, while others lack practical implementation details.

In summary, reliability of the AI/ML model in beam management is important, as failure can lead to degraded quality of service. In other words, the reliability of the AI/ML model in beam management is necessary to maintain quality of service in 3GPP networks. Failure in these models can lead to significant performance degradation, and therefore implementation of a robust rollback mechanism is required to transition to non-AI/ML methods when model performance is below a defined threshold. Thus, a robust fallback mechanism is needed to switch to other methods for beam management when model performance is inadequate, and a method for ensuring that model failure is timely and accurately detected, and allowing seamless switching to maintain quality of service and minimize disruption is needed. Future improvements may be focused on systems that ensure seamless handover, particularly in dynamic environments.

As shown in fig. 2, the terminal device 101 sends (205) to the first network device 102 the operating conditions of the terminal device within a monitoring window over which the performance metrics of the AI/ML model are aggregated and evaluated. The first network device 102 receives (210) an operating condition of the terminal device 101 within a monitoring window. The first network device 102 sends (215) the operating conditions and the performance metrics of the AL/ML model to the second network device 103 within the monitoring window. The second network device 103 receives (220) the operating conditions within the monitoring window and the performance metrics of the AI/ML model within the monitoring window.

The second network device 103 then determines (225) at least one threshold value for evaluating a performance metric of the AI/ML model based on the operating conditions and the historical performance data of the AI/ML model. The second network device 103 determines (230) whether the AI/ML model failed based on a comparison between the performance metric and at least one threshold. The second network device 103 then sends (235) a result to the first network device 102 as to whether the AI/ML model failed, and the result is based on a comparison between the performance metric and at least one threshold. The first network device 102 receives (240) a result regarding whether the AI/ML model failed. The first network device 102 then sends (245) a result to the terminal device 101 as to whether the AI/ML model failed. The terminal device 101 then receives (250) a result from the first network device 102 as to whether the AI/ML model failed.

Through process 200, the operating conditions of the terminal device may be transmitted to the network device within a monitoring window over which performance metrics of the AI/ML model are aggregated and evaluated. Instead of a single observation, the performance metrics of the AI/ML model are aggregated and evaluated over a monitoring window. The threshold value for evaluating the performance metric of the AI/ML model may be dynamically determined by the network function entity (e.g., the second network device 103) based on the current operating conditions and historical performance data of the AI/ML model. Thus, instead of a static threshold for model failure, the solution would implement a calibration mechanism that adjusts the threshold based on historical performance data and current operating conditions. For example, if the UE is in a high mobility scenario, the threshold for switching to a non-AI/ML method may be set lower to account for the increased likelihood of model inaccuracy. The results regarding whether the AI/ML model failed may then be determined, for example, by the network function entity based on a comparison between the dynamically determined threshold and the performance metric. The result may then be sent to the terminal device.

Since reliability of AI/ML models in beam management is important, as failure can lead to degraded quality of service, the process provides a method for ensuring that a UE can effectively verify the applicability of a model based on multiple observations by including dynamically defining thresholds for model failure and monitoring performance over time. Then, switching to other methods (e.g., non-AI/ML methods) may be performed by the terminal device based on the result of AI/ML model failure.
